title: SOC2 sidecar notes — evidence mapping & quick wins
content:
Purpose: quick informal record for sidecar thinking — not polished. Use this to capture small evidence hunts, ideas for automating evidence, and talking points for the next SOC2 sync.

Snapshot / context:
- Goal: get top-20 control evidence mature enough for internal audit by end of Q2 2026. Focus first on logical access, change management, backup/restore, and incident response.
- Constraints: limited SRE cycles, infra work prioritized for product launches in April. Need low-effort wins.

Quick wins (low lift):
1) IAM access report (week-of Mar 8)
   - Action: generate daily CSV export of service accounts with admin scope from GCP project(s). Script: infra/scripts/iam-audit-export.sh (PR referenced above).
   - Owner: Jordan. Evidence: dated CSV + small README that describes query.
   - Risk note: must redact user emails for shared evidence pack.

2) Backup verification for DB snapshots (ongoing)
   - Current: daily snapshots configured but no monthly restore test evidence.
   - Proposed: schedule a monthly quick-restore run in staging -> record runbook steps and duration.
   - Owner: Ellie. Evidence: restore run log + screenshot of data restored + timestamp.

Control mapping rough (brain dump):
- CC6 (Logical Access) -> evidence: IAM CSV, role binding change history, SSO logs (Okta).
- CC7 (Change Mgmt) -> evidence: merge-to-main policy + CI check screenshot, PR reviewer list, CHG ticket IDs (Jira).
- CC9 (System Ops/Monitoring) -> evidence: Datadog alert runbook links, SLO dashboard screenshots, incident postmortems for prior 12 months.
- CC11 (Backup/Recovery) -> evidence: snapshot policy docs, restore test logs, retention config.

Open questions / things to verify:
- Can we pull a trustable changelog for infra terraform changes? (terraform state + git history isn't sufficient for approved change evidence). Possible approach: require a Jira ticket link in PR template and use a GitHub Action to block merges without a ticket.
- How to show segregation of duties for small infra team? Need matrix showing who can approve vs who can deploy. Might use an internal google sheet + signed-off email chain as interim evidence.

Notes from quick sync 2026-02-26 10:30am with Jordan/Ellie:
- Jordan: will prototype IAM CSV export that contains last-used timestamp per service account, plan to run daily and keep 90-day history.
- Ellie: will run a manual restore in staging by Mar 12 and capture logs.
- Ramya: will draft a short playbook for evidence packaging and checklist so auditors can find artifacts quickly.
- Next sync: Mar 18, aim to have 3 evidence items packaged.

Automation ideas (medium lift but reusable):
- Evidence aggregator lambda: ingest CSV/logs/screenshots and push to secure S3 folder with JSON index (date, control id, owner, links). Minimal UI: static index page served to auditors (read-only).
- GitHub Action: validate PR template contains jira ticket and control tags (e.g., control:CC7). If missing, fail status. Helps map changes to controls over time.

Potential evidence gaps (priority):
- MFA enforcement proof for service accounts (how to show service token rotation?)
- Formal change approval trace for infra config changes older than 6 months (retro evidence needed)
- Retention/backup of logs: need documented retention policy + sample export of logs covering a 6-month window.

Immediate TODOs (priority ordering):
- [ ] Jordan: drop prototype IAM CSV to shared drive and link in Confluence (due Mar 8)
- [ ] Ellie: run restore in staging and write short restore log (due Mar 12)
- [ ] Ramya: create evidence packaging checklist doc + sample zip structure (due Mar 15)
- [ ] Team: pick one control to fully automate evidence collection by end of Mar (candidate: CC6 or CC11)

Brainstorm fragments (notes-to-self):
- "evidence packaging" = folder/%Y-%m-%d/control-CC6/README.md + artifacts (csv, screenshot, signer.txt). Keep names consistent.
- Consider a short video walkthrough (30–60s) for complex evidence: e.g., click through the dashboard that shows SLO. Embed in index as mp4.
- Audit-friendly filenames: 2026-03-12_CC11_restore-log-ellie.txt (timestamped, owner initial).

Risks (quick assessment):
- If we rely on ad-hoc screenshots, repeatability is low; prefer exports/logs.
- Small team -> SOD limited; need compensating controls (team rotation, mandatory code review, CI gating).

Reference snippets / quick commands:
- IAM export (prototype): gcloud iam service-accounts list --format=json > sa-list.json  # then filter roles bindings via gcloud projects get-iam-policy
- example GH action check (pseudo): if (!contains(pr.body, /JIRA-/)) fail

Last thoughts: keep this as informal 'sidecar' notebook — it's where I dump half-baked ideas before formalizing in Confluence. When something stabilizes, we'll move it to confluence under /SEC/Control-Mapping and update linked_artifacts.

-- end --
